clue.text: Writer, mostly haughty when seen on street

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: haughty means proud, stuck-up

explanation.surface: A writer who looks rather snooty whenever spotted out on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was a French novelist, author of In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Broadcast favouring assertion

parts.note: to be pro something is to be in favour of it
a claim is an assertion

explanation.surface: A broadcast that comes out in favour of some assertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast news is to announce it publicly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Hidden within moor, pink plant

indicators.note: Hidden within says the letters lie concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Somewhere on the moor a pink flower is tucked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpine (also orpin) is a succulent plant of the stonecrop family with pinkish flowers.

clue.text: The prose mostly inappropriate? Bit of poetry called for

indicators.note: inappropriate suggests the letters are out of their proper places
mostly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Prose turning out unsuitable, so some verse is wanted instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts PROSE to PROS; 'inappropriate' rearranges THE plus PROS.
explanation.definitionFit: A strophe is a stanza, originally a section of a chorus's song in Greek drama.

clue.text: Ghosts — sort primarily associated with hell?

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word it follows

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth, so hell

explanation.surface: Asking whether spirits are the kind one links with the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are spirits of the dead, especially in classical literature.

clue.text: One adds decoration to a tile

definitions.text: One adds decoration to a tile

parts.words: One adds decoration to a tile
parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat, so the thing that decorates one is a ribbon round its crown

explanation.surface: Someone ornamenting a roof or floor tile.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatband is the decorative ribbon encircling the crown of a hat.

clue.text: Comes across dossier with CV falsified

indicators.note: falsified suggests the letters have been tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a file containing a doctored CV.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across something is to find it, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Holy type at university I would put down as 'laughable'

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy person
a student in residence is said to be up at university
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A saint up at university, dismissed by me as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stupid is foolish enough to be ridiculous, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Leader holds river game in much bigger water area

indicators.note: holds means the first word contains the others

parts.note: a boss is a leader or manager
the Po is Italy's longest river
RU is rugby union, a fifteen-a-side game

explanation.surface: A chief taking part in a river sport within some vast stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bosporus links the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, a far larger expanse than the river in the surface; 'holds' puts the river and the game inside the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bosporus is the strait joining the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, a far bigger body of water than a river.

clue.text: Peaceful army overcoming vandals, nasty men in capital city

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, a charitable army

indicators.note: nasty suggests the vandals' letters are mangled

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A pacifist force defeating a gang of vile vandals in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' turns VANDALS into NSALVAD, which goes below SA and above OR.
explanation.definitionFit: San Salvador is the capital of El Salvador in Central America.

clue.text: Spot us involved in chancy exercise

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled up together

explanation.surface: Picking us out is a matter of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is a situation decided by chance, like a coin toss.

clue.text: Engineer in factory wasting time

indicators.note: wasting means that piece is lost from the word

parts.note: a plant is a factory

explanation.surface: An engineer in a works squandering hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer an outcome is to plan it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Description of scale that could be found in ancient pot

indicators.note: could be found in suggests the answer lies within the letters once they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical scale's name turning up inside an old pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentatonic scale is a musical scale of five notes to the octave.

clue.text: Row about divine female and theologian immersed in drink — it's nonsense!

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a file is a row of people one behind another
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine or clergyman

indicators.note: immersed in places one piece inside another

parts.note: ale is a drink
DD, Doctor of Divinity, denotes a theologian

explanation.surface: A quarrel over a goddess and a churchman sunk in drink is called rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row about divine' builds the first half and 'female and theologian immersed in drink' the second; a divine is a clergyman, so the same doctorate abbreviation serves both.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddle-faddle is trivial talk or fuss, an old word for twaddle.

clue.text: One spews out rubbish, spoiling river dell

indicators.note: spoiling suggests the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone dumping waste and ruining a river valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveller is someone who talks silly nonsense.

clue.text: Edmund's put away inside to be spruced up

indicators.note: inside means the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edmund
to put away food is to have eaten it

explanation.surface: Edmund has a meal stowed away to make himself look smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatened means tidied, made neat, a past-participle synonym.

clue.text: Little devil in charge of one small building deprived of necessities?

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
to be over something is to be in charge of it
I is the Roman numeral for one
a shed is a small building

explanation.surface: An imp managing a single hut finds itself without basic needs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impoverished is to be reduced to poverty, lacking essentials.

clue.text: Excuse of an era preceding electronic messages?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix for before
text is the word for SMS messages sent by phone

explanation.surface: An excuse dating from the days before people sent texts.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also reads as pre-text, the era before texting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretext is a false reason given to hide the real one.

clue.text: Emphasise good news about lost sheep?

definitions.meaning: to drive a point forcefully is to stress it hard
a male sheep that strayed is back at the farm

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: the male sheep is home.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram home a point is to stress it forcibly, an idiom; read literally, a male sheep is back.

clue.text: Engineers leading rebellion get back

indicators.note: leading means the first piece comes in front of the second

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a coup is an uprising that seizes power

explanation.surface: Engineers heading an uprising to retake something.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover a loss, to get it back.

clue.text: Hesitation about loud rude men spoiling democratic procedure

indicators.note: about here means the hesitation word is turned around

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: spoiling suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Doubts over noisy, rude men wrecking a public vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ER into RE; 'spoiling' rearranges RUDE MEN into ERENDUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum is a direct vote by the electorate on a single question.

clue.text: It's a bit of a fag being laughed at

definitions.text: It's a bit of a fag
definitions.meaning: fag is British slang for a cigarette, and this is its unsmoked stub
this is the one who is the target of ridicule

explanation.walkthrough: 'fag' is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is a cigarette end, and also the target of jokes.

clue.text: Dog nibbled companion

parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite, so nibbled
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A dog gave its friend a nip.
explanation.definitionFit: A female dog is called by this name.

clue.text: Man entering pit shortly finds dog

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner who goes down the pit

explanation.surface: A miner going underground soon discovers a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a sheepdog breed from Scotland.

clue.text: Aussie beast has pain sitting down

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, an Australian animal
a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: A kangaroo feeling sore when it sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosting is settling on a perch to rest, as birds do.

clue.text: One intercepting gas is a sort of thief

indicators.note: intercepting means the first piece cuts into the second

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly, to prate
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who taps a gas supply is a kind of robber.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate robs ships at sea, or copies others' work without permission.

clue.text: The rioting gets in the way of modern rule

indicators.note: gets in the way of reads as gets inside, putting one piece within another
rioting suggests the letters run wild

explanation.surface: Rioters obstructing a contemporary regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in the way of' reads cryptically as getting inside, and 'rioting' signals the anagram of The; 'rule' is the definition, not part of the mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a systematic procedure or rule for doing something.
